results.title: Introduction to Scribe in Willow | Willow Voice Help Center
results.content:
### 2. Respond with Scribe

Activate Scribe and say what you want to say. Scribe reads what's on your screen and understands the full context of what you're responding to. This context helps Scribe write your response with your input.  
​  
It writes the reply right where your cursor is.   
​

Example 1: Replying to an email about a meeting time

The email thread on your screen says:

```
"What time works for you tomorrow? I was thinking 7 PM at Starbucks."
```

What you say:

```
"Say, yes, that works."
```

What Scribe writes:

```
Yes, 7 PM at Starbucks works perfectly for me. See you tomorrow!  
  
Best,   
John
```

Example 2: Responding to feedback on a doc  
​

A teammate left a comment:

```
"This section feels a little long, can we tighten it up?"
```

What you say: [...] ## Final Notes: Just Try It

The easiest way to learn Scribe is to use it on the work you're already doing.

If you spend a lot of your day in email, Slack, or communication platforms, start there.

You don't have to use ChatGPT or Claude to write or rewrite text for you anymore. Press your Scribe hotkey, describe what you want to say, and watch how well it writes it for you.

Scribe is a new way to communicate. Instead of dictating word-for-word, you can describe what you want to say and Scribe writes it for you in your style and context.

Written by Allan Guo

Table of contents

## What's the Difference Between Dictation and Scribe?

 Dictation is what most people think of when they hear "voice typing." You speak exactly what you want written, word-for-word. Willow transcribes it. It's faster than typing, but you still have to find every word yourself.
 Scribe is different. You speak your intent, and Scribe writes the message for you. You don't need to figure out the words before you start. You just brain dump what you want to communicate. Scribe handles the writing, formatting, and tone.
